  "raw_idea": "Multi‑hop question answering often relies on reasoning over a chain of facts in a knowledge graph, yet current language‑model training typically uses isolated head‑relation‑tail triples, depriving the model of the surrounding context that supports multi‑step inference. We propose to enrich each target triple (or path) with additional triples drawn from the same source passage, forming a local context subgraph that is presented together with the primary supervision signal. The model will be fine‑tuned under two regimes: one using only the target triple/path and another that also incorporates the supporting context. To improve the reliability of the base facts, we will introduce an adaptive repair loop that detects one‑hop failures, generates corrective examples, and iteratively refines the model. input.problem: Language models used for multi-hop question answering over knowledge graphs (KGs) are typically trained on isolated head-relation-tail triples (or single relation paths). This strips away the passage-level context — the neighbouring triples that co-occur with the target fact — that supports multi-step inference. Two coupled deficiencies result: (1) the supervision signal is context-poor, so the model must learn to chain facts without seeing the local evidence that makes chaining plausible; and (2) the base facts themselves may be noisy or incompletely grounded, so errors at one hop propagate and compound over longer reasoning chains.
input.target_domain: Knowledge-graph-based multi-hop question answering (KGQA) and KG-augmented/grounded language-model training (graph-to-text, structured knowledge grounding).
input.proposed_method: Three stacked components. (A) Context-enriched supervision: for each target triple or target path, retrieve additional triples that were extracted from the same source passage and present them as a "local context subgraph" together with the primary supervision signal during fine-tuning; compare an isolated-triple regime against a context-augmented regime under matched data/token budgets. (B) Adaptive repair loop: detect one-hop failures, generate corrective examples from them, and iteratively refine the model before the multi-hop stage. (C) RL stage: apply reinforcement-learning-based optimization on lower-hop QA instances, then evaluate transfer to deeper multi-hop queries.
input.hypothesis: Fine-tuning with passage-coherent local context subgraphs around each target triple/path yields higher multi-hop QA accuracy and better transfer to higher-hop questions than isolated-triple supervision at matched token and optimization-step budgets. Adding an adaptive one-hop-failure repair loop further improves base-fact reliability and therefore multi-hop accuracy beyond context enrichment alone; RL on lower-hop instances improves rather than degrades deeper-hop transfer.
input.research_question: Does fine-tuning a language model with passage-derived local context subgraphs around each target triple/path, compared with isolated-triple supervision at matched token and optimization-step budgets, improve multi-hop KGQA answer accuracy and transfer to higher-hop questions, and does an adaptive one-hop-failure repair loop add measurable gains beyond context enrichment alone?
input.expected_contribution: A controlled empirical characterization of whether passage-level context around target triples is the active ingredient in multi-hop KGQA training (as opposed to more tokens/compute), an adaptive repair procedure for one-hop failures, and evidence on whether low-hop RL training transfers to deeper-hop queries — with an honest report on where the approach reduces to existing subgraph-retrieval or KG-grounded training methods.
input.target_system: A knowledge-graph-grounded language model (encoder-decoder or decoder-only) fine-tuned to answer questions from triples/subgraphs, evaluated on multi-hop QA benchmarks with KG evidence. Base model, KG source and passage alignment to be fixed by the experiment plan.

knowledge graph augmented language model pretraining triple knowledge injection
reinforcement learning multi-hop knowledge graph question answering weak supervision
context-enriched fact supervision graph-to-text multi-hop reasoning
passage-level knowledge graph triple extraction context-aware KGQA training
subgraph retrieval enhanced multi-hop knowledge base question answering
assumptions: Each target triple/path can be associated with a source passage from which additional co-occurring triples can be drawn (i.e., the KG is passage-aligned or was constructed from text).

One-hop failures are detectable with a measurable signal (e.g., error on single-hop questions or low confidence on a decomposable sub-question), and corrective training examples can be generated automatically.
The same relation/entity inventory is shared between lower-hop training instances and deeper multi-hop test queries, so transfer is well-defined.
Gains from context enrichment will be assessed against a token/compute-matched isolated-triple control, otherwise improvements cannot be attributed to context.
The base language model, KG, and fine-tuning hyperparameters are held fixed across regime comparisons.

controls: Total fine-tuning tokens and optimization steps
dependent: Multi-hop answer accuracy (EM / F1) on held-out multi-hop QA
Single-hop (one-hop) accuracy used as the failure signal
Transfer accuracy at increasing hop depth (2-hop, 3-hop, ...)
Path/evidence faithfulness (whether predicted reasoning path matches gold evidence)
Training token/compute cost (to enable matched-budget comparison)
independent: Supervision regime: isolated triple/path vs. passage-derived local context subgraph
Repair loop: off vs. on (with count of iterations as a factor)
RL stage: off vs. on, and hop depth of the instances used for RL (1-hop, 2-hop)
Number of context triples included (context budget)

ambiguities.question: Which evaluation metric should be the primary dependent variable (answer EM/F1 vs. path hits@k vs. evidence faithfulness)?
ambiguities.resolution: Use standard multi-hop QA answer metrics (EM and F1), with path/evidence faithfulness as a secondary metric; these are the dominant metrics in the retrieved multi-hop QA benchmark literature.

ambiguities.question: Which benchmark(s) and workload should be used?
ambiguities.resolution: Candidate multi-hop QA benchmarks in the retrieved literature include 2WikiMultiHopQA (arxiv:2011.01060), MoreHopQA (arxiv:2406.13397), HotpotQA-style passage/KG multi-hop sets, and KGQA sets used by subgraph-retrieval work (arxiv:2202.13296, doi:10.18653/v1/2020.emnlp-main.99). Final dataset choice is deferred to the experiment plan; benchmark must expose hop depth and gold evidence/paths.

ambiguities.question: Which base language model and KG should be used?
What exactly counts as 'the same source passage' when the KG is not passage-aligned?
Is the RL stage additive over context enrichment plus repair, or does it collapse to standard path-walking RL that already exists?
What constitutes an automatic 'one-hop failure' detection rule, and how are corrective examples generated?

questions: Is there prior work that already trains language models with passage-context-enriched KG triples/subgraphs for multi-hop QA, and how close is it to the proposed method and evaluation?
Are reported gains from subgraph/context augmentation attributable to added context structure or merely to additional tokens/compute (the matched-budget confounder)?
Does a training-time repair loop over detected one-hop failures measurably improve multi-hop accuracy over no repair, and over a simpler data-cleaning baseline?
Does RL optimization on lower-hop QA instances transfer to higher-hop queries, or does it overfit the low-hop distribution?
What benchmarks, metrics and hop-depth splits are standard for measuring deeper-hop transfer in KGQA?

input.question: Has context-enriched (passage-local subgraph) triple supervision for multi-hop KGQA already been proposed and evaluated, so that the proposed mechanism is largely covered by existing subgraph-retrieval or KG-grounded training work?
input.description: Subgraph retrieval enhanced KBQA (arxiv:2202.13296), GraftNet (doi:10.18653/v1/2020.emnlp-main.99) and subgraph retrieval/link scoring for multi-hop QA (doi:10.1007/s10489-024-05935-8) already use multi-triple subgraphs rather than isolated triples at inference/training time. The idea's distinguishing claim — that the subgraph is drawn from the SAME source passage and used as a training-time supervision enrichment at matched budget — needs to be checked against these.
input.rationale: If the mechanism and evaluation are already covered, the contribution reduces to a replication; overlap must be established before investing in the experiment plan.

input.question: Could any observed gain from context enrichment be explained by the extra context tokens/compute rather than by passage-coherent structure, i.e. is the comparison confounded?
input.description: The context-augmented regime presents more tokens than the isolated-triple regime. Without a token-matched control (e.g., random/sampled distractor triples from other passages, or repeated target triple to reach equal token count), a gain cannot be attributed to passage coherence. This is the most dangerous confounder for the idea's central claim.
input.rationale: The idea's core claim is that context structure, not volume, is the active ingredient; the naive two-regime comparison does not isolate this.

input.question: Does RL optimization on lower-hop QA instances actually transfer to deeper multi-hop queries, or does it overfit the low-hop distribution and hurt deeper hops?
input.description: The idea assumes that cleaning/training on lower-hop instances transfers upward. RL path-walking literature (DeepPath doi:10.18653/v1/d17-1060, reward shaping doi:10.18653/v1/d18-1362, intermediate supervision arxiv:2101.03737) suggests gains depend heavily on intermediate/long-horizon supervision, and reward sparsity grows with hop depth. No retrieved paper was checked for hop-depth transfer specifically.
input.rationale: If transfer fails, the RL component of the pipeline is unjustified and the contribution must be narrowed to context enrichment plus repair.

input.question: Is passage-level triple co-occurrence (a local context subgraph) reliably available for the target facts in standard multi-hop KGQA datasets?
input.description: The mechanism requires that additional triples can be drawn 'from the same source passage' as the target triple/path. Passage-aligned KGs (text-derived) support this; curated KGs used in KGQA (e.g. Freebase-style) may not have per-triple provenance. Retrieval-augmented KGQA work (doi:10.20944/preprints202505.1992.v1, arxiv:2607.23278) suggests graph+text sources exist, but provenance granularity must be verified for the chosen dataset.
input.rationale: If provenance is absent, the operational definition of 'local context subgraph' must fall back to graph neighbourhood, changing what the method actually tests.

input.question: Which benchmark and metric split best isolates transfer to deeper hops (e.g. accuracy as a function of hop depth on 2WikiMultiHopQA / MoreHopQA / HotpotQA-style sets)?
input.description: The claim of transfer to deeper multi-hop queries needs a hop-depth-stratified evaluation. Retrieved benchmarks 2WikiMultiHopQA (arxiv:2011.01060) and MoreHopQA (arxiv:2406.13397) explicitly address comprehensive reasoning-step evaluation, but the exact stratification and the metric (EM vs F1 vs faithfulness) still need to be fixed.
input.rationale: Without hop-depth stratification the central 'deeper transfer' claim is untestable and could be an artifact of aggregate accuracy.
